claims.text: HEAs have superior resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in harsh environments.
Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion is governed by the ability to rapidly form and maintain a stable, multi-component passive oxide layer.
Intrinsic compositional heterogeneity and lattice distortion in HEAs enhance the passive oxide layer.
The passive oxide layer self-heals during mechanical wear.
Self-healing of the passive layer reduces overall material degradation.
The proposed initial material is an equilibrated, near-equiatomic HEA containing multiple principal elements.
The initial HEA surface has a naturally formed thin passive oxide film.
Underlying microstructural heterogeneity and lattice distortion support the integrity of the multi-component passive oxide layer.
Compositional complexity in HEAs promotes formation of a mixed oxide layer.
The mixed oxide layer formed by HEAs is more chemically stable and mechanically robust than a simpler oxide layer.
Abundant reactive elements rapidly repair minor wear damage through in-situ oxidation.
Rapid oxide repair minimizes exposure of the underlying metal to corrosive agents and thereby reduces corrosion rates.
The balance between oxide formation and mechanically driven oxide removal produces synergistic resistance to degradation.
Under matched wear-corrosion conditions, the HEA will have a significantly lower combined degradation rate than conventional stainless steel.
Relative to conventional stainless steel, the HEA will exhibit less wear-related material loss.
Relative to conventional stainless steel, the HEA will exhibit slower corrosion kinetics.
The HEA passive film will remain more intact and recover rapidly after mechanical perturbation.
Conventional stainless steel forms a simpler and less adaptable passive oxide film than the proposed HEA.
The predicted protection should hold when wear is moderate enough to permit oxide self-healing.
The protective effect may fail when oxide removal outpaces repair or when the environment chemically destabilizes the oxide, such as at very low pH or under highly oxidative conditions.
